title: Minimal CI/CD System from Scratch with Build Agents
problem: Relying on black-box hosted CI/CD services obscures the fundamental distributed systems principles required to build scalable, secure continuous integration infrastructure. Multi-tenant build systems must parse pipeline definitions, schedule directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks across worker pools, enforce process isolation between untrusted build jobs, stream live terminal logs without memory leaks, and persist artifacts securely. This project implements a custom containerized CI/CD engine in Go consisting of a central job scheduler server and autonomous worker agents that execute pipeline stages in isolated Docker containers with live WebSocket log streaming.
use_cases: Air-gapped and self-hosted build automation for regulated enterprise environments
High-performance continuous integration runner with localized Docker layer caching
Lightweight task orchestration engine for automated test execution and artifact bundling
hard_parts: Parsing pipeline definitions into directed acyclic graphs and scheduling parallel tasks without deadlock
Managing Docker container lifecycles safely on worker nodes to prevent zombie containers upon job cancellation
Streaming high-volume stdout and stderr terminal logs over WebSockets without unbounded memory buffers
Enforcing secure agent-to-server communication and mutual authentication across untrusted networks
screener_signals: Modular Go architecture cleanly separating controller scheduler from worker execution daemons
Deterministic DAG scheduler executing parallel stages with topological sort verification
Anti-fake verification script running dynamic job specifications and validating live log output streams

stack.role: core implementation language for scheduler server, agent daemon, and CLI tool
container engine providing hermetic process isolation for build job steps
lightweight transactional database storing pipeline runs, stages, and agent states
bidirectional real-time protocol for task dispatch and live terminal log streaming

components.name: Pipeline DAG Engine
components.purpose: Parses YAML pipeline specifications into dependency graphs and validates topological execution order

components.name: Central Scheduler Server
components.purpose: Manages job queues, persists pipeline execution history, and assigns ready tasks to available agents

components.name: Worker Execution Agent
components.purpose: Pulls assigned tasks, spawns isolated Docker worker containers, and monitors container exit status

components.name: Log Streaming Daemon
components.purpose: Captures container stdout and stderr streams and broadcasts live chunks to connected clients

architecture.data_flow: Users submit a pipeline YAML file via CLI; the DAG Engine resolves task dependencies; the Scheduler persists stages in SQLite and enqueues root tasks; an available Worker Agent claims the task via WebSockets; the agent spawns an isolated Docker container with the specified image; container logs stream in real-time over WebSockets to the server; upon container exit, the agent reports exit codes, triggering subsequent dependent tasks.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Container resource limits enforce CPU and memory boundaries; timeout watchdog terminates hung containers after configured duration.

targets.method: Verification of topological stage execution order across complex dependency graphs
targets.input: 20 test pipeline specifications with parallel branches, join stages, and sequential dependencies
targets.minimum_pass: 20 of 20 test pipelines execute stages in strict dependency order with 0 race conditions
targets.target: 20 of 20 test pipelines execute stages in strict dependency order with 0 race conditions
targets.report: Unit test execution output and stage execution timestamp logs

targets.method: Measurement of time elapsed between pipeline cancellation command and container destruction
targets.input: Running build job executing infinite loop inside Docker worker container
targets.minimum_pass: Worker container stopped and removed within 4.0 seconds of cancellation signal
targets.target: Worker container stopped and removed within 1.5 seconds of cancellation signal
targets.report: Docker daemon event log confirming container kill and rm events

targets.method: Measurement of latency from container stdout write to WebSocket client delivery
targets.input: Synthetic build job emitting 5,000 log lines at 500 lines per second
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, local loopback network
targets.minimum_pass: p95 log transmission latency < 80ms without dropped lines
targets.target: p95 log transmission latency < 35ms without dropped lines
targets.report: Benchmark log analyzer reporting packet send and receive timestamps

starter_input.spec: YAML pipeline schema specification and collection of test build definitions covering lint, test, and build stages.
starter_input.size: 5 test pipeline definitions ranging from simple single-step jobs to complex multi-stage fan-out/fan-in DAGs
starter_input.seeded_cases: Cyclic dependency graphs, failing intermediate stages, runaway memory jobs, and abrupt agent disconnects
starter_input.label_source: Deterministic Go test fixtures and expected exit status assertions
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly synthetic build commands (echo, test mocks, sleep); zero real credentials or repository code used

prerequisites: Intermediate Go programming (goroutines, channels, network sockets, context cancellation)
Familiarity with Docker container APIs and volume mounts
Basic understanding of graph algorithms (directed acyclic graphs, topological sorting)

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-bound build job execution)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Go 1.21+ and Docker Engine installed
environment.fallback_path: Local shell execution runner without Docker if Docker socket permissions are restricted

riskiest_component.name: Dangling Zombie Docker Containers upon Abrupt Agent Termination
riskiest_component.fallback: Implement an automated reaper process on server startup that labels and prunes orphaned runner containers

rubric.expected_result: DAG scheduler parses steps and outputs valid topological execution plan
rubric.pass_criterion: All scheduler unit tests pass with exit code 0

rubric.input: Pipeline run execution via CLI ./bin/ci run fixtures/build_job.yaml
rubric.action: Inspect Docker container lifecycle on worker host
rubric.expected_result: Worker spawns container, runs commands, captures stdout, and removes container on completion
rubric.evidence_location: CLI terminal output and docker ps -a log
rubric.pass_criterion: Build completes successfully with exit code 0 and container removed from host

rubric.input: Active running build job canceled via ./bin/ci cancel <job-id>
rubric.expected_result: Worker intercepts cancellation and forcibly destroys container within 4 seconds
rubric.evidence_location: Agent log file and Docker daemon event stream
rubric.pass_criterion: Container state transitions to destroyed within 4 seconds with 0 leftover containers

rubric.input: 5,000 log lines emitted by worker container
rubric.expected_result: Log streaming client receives all lines in sequential order with p95 latency < 80ms
rubric.pass_criterion: Total received line count equals 5,000 with 0 dropped lines

rubric.input: Dynamic echo token generated at runtime by verification script
rubric.expected_result: Server schedules job, agent executes echo command in clean container, and returns matching token in log stream
rubric.pass_criterion: Execution log matches dynamic token with exit status 0

worksheet.q1: The student builds a containerized CI/CD system in Go consisting of a DAG task scheduler, a worker agent daemon executing steps in isolated Docker containers, and WebSocket log streaming.
worksheet.q2: Core path: YAML parser, DAG scheduler, Docker worker isolation, WebSocket log streaming, and cancellation cleanup (34h). Extended path: S3 artifact store and GitHub webhook receiver (+15h).
worksheet.q3: Components: DAG Parser (5h), Docker Runner (8h), WebSocket Protocol (5h), SQLite Queuing (4h), Log Streaming (4h), Docs & Buffer (4h). Total 30h x 1.15 = 34.5 -> 34h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: CI/CD/DevOps/security pipelines, CLI/tools/libraries. Metrics: DAG Execution Adherence, Container Cleanup Duration, Log Streaming Latency. Rejected: SQL query execution plans (not an analytical database).
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: DAG cycle detection and topological sorting, Docker container cleanup on cancellation, WebSocket memory buffering, and agent authentication.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 5 YAML pipeline definitions covering parallel stages, cyclic errors, and failing tests. No real user data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local shell runner without Docker.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Dangling zombie Docker containers. Fallback: startup container reaper process.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static mocked logs. Anti-fake check 5 passes a dynamic token at runtime and asserts live container execution and token logging.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local Docker container execution only.
